prompts.display_text: Pin a country where Church Global Histories record a branch of the Church organized before 1847
prompts.text_original: A country where, per Church Global Histories, a branch of the Church was organized before the pioneers left Nauvoo in 1846 and 1847.
prompts.citation: Church Global Histories chronologies: United States, Canada, England, Australia, Germany
prompts.note: Ireland does not count: the 1840 Hillsborough branch is in Northern Ireland, part of the United Kingdom.
prompts.summary: Before the exodus west, the Church was already more than an American church. Global Histories record a branch at Ernestown, Canada in 1832, Preston, England in 1837, Darmstadt, Germany in 1843, and Montefiores in South Australia in 1844.

answers.name: United States
answers.fact: 1830: the Church was organized in New York; branches followed across the states.

answers.name: Canada
answers.fact: 1832: a branch was organized at Ernestown, Upper Canada.

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: 1837: a branch was organized at Preston, England; by 1840 there were branches in Scotland, Wales and at Hillsborough in Northern Ireland.

answers.name: Australia
answers.fact: 1844: a branch was organized at Montefiores near Adelaide.

answers.name: Germany
answers.fact: 1843: Johann Greenig, a German convert baptized in the United States, preached in Darmstadt and reported establishing the first branch in Germany.

prompts.display_text: Pin a European country where a current General Authority Seventy once led a mission (as of October 2026).
prompts.text_original: As of October 2026, several General Authority Seventies had led missions in Europe as mission presidents. Pin a European country where one of those missions was headquartered, as named in the Church's official biographies.
prompts.summary: Many General Authority Seventies first led missions. As of October 2026, they had led European missions in England, France, Spain, Portugal, Germany, Russia, Ukraine, the Czech Republic and Slovakia, and Slovenia and Croatia. Elder Jorg Klebingat, born in Germany, presided in Kyiv, Ukraine.

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: England London Mission (Elder Sinclair) and England Manchester Mission (Elder Peter M. Johnson).

answers.name: Germany
answers.fact: Elder Michael Cziesla was interim president of the Germany Frankfurt Mission in 2020.

answers.name: Spain
answers.fact: Spain Barcelona Mission (Elder Villar).

answers.name: France
answers.fact: France Lyon Mission (Elder Giraud-Carrier).

answers.name: Portugal
answers.fact: Elder Ronald M. Barcellos was called as a mission leader in Portugal in 2021.

answers.name: Russia
answers.fact: Elder Paul B. Pieper and his wife were mission leaders in St. Petersburg.

answers.name: Ukraine
answers.fact: Ukraine Kyiv Mission (Elder Klebingat).

answers.name: Czech Republic
answers.fact: Czech/Slovak Mission, based in Prague, 2013 to 2016 (Elder McConkie).

answers.name: Croatia
answers.fact: The Slovenia/Croatia Mission that Elder Rowe led from 2011 also covered Croatia.

answers.name: Slovakia
answers.fact: The Czech/Slovak Mission that Elder McConkie led, 2013 to 2016, also covered Slovakia.

answers.name: Slovenia
answers.fact: Elder Edward B. Rowe was called in 2011 to lead the Slovenia/Croatia Mission, based in Ljubljana.

prompts.display_text: Pin an African country where Latter-day Saint converts were baptized before 1955.
prompts.text_original: Before 1955, Latter-day Saint converts had been baptized in only a few African countries, mostly through the South African Mission. Pin a country where, according to the Church Global Histories, converts were baptized before 1955.
prompts.citation: Global Histories chronologies (South Africa, Mauritius, Namibia, Zimbabwe, Zambia)
prompts.note: Nigeria is not scored: a request for missionaries was sent in 1946, but no baptisms are recorded before 1955.
prompts.summary: Missionaries reached Cape Town in 1853 and organized the first branch in Africa at Mowbray. A convert from South Africa baptized six people in Mauritius in 1856. In the 1900s the South African Mission reached members in South West Africa and the Rhodesias, today Namibia, Zimbabwe and Zambia.

answers.name: South Africa
answers.fact: Joseph Patterson and John Dodel, the first converts in South Africa, were baptized at Mowbray, Cape Town, May 26, 1853.

answers.name: Zambia
answers.fact: Johanna and William A. Jubber Jr. were baptized at Ndola in 1947.

answers.name: Zimbabwe
answers.fact: In 1928 near Shangani, Southern Rhodesia, the Jubber family invited mission leaders to baptize their sons.

answers.name: Mauritius
answers.fact: George F. W. Kershaw baptized six converts during a 1856 mission.

answers.name: Namibia
answers.fact: Lawrence C. Ratcliff baptized Johannes and Martha Cloete at Karibib in 1928.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country where Jesus's family or his disciples fled or were sent to escape danger, in Matthew or Acts
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a place where Jesus's family or his followers fled, or were sent, to escape danger, in Matthew or Acts
prompts.note: Antioch of Syria is today Antakya in Turkey, so it counts for Turkey, not Syria. Samaria is in the West Bank (Palestine).
prompts.summary: Danger kept scattering the faithful, and the gospel went with them. Joseph took Jesus into Egypt to escape Herod. After Stephen was stoned, disciples fled through Judea and Samaria and on to Phenice, Cyprus and Antioch. Paul was later rushed by night to Tarsus, Berea, Athens and Caesarea.

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Joseph took the young child and Mary by night into Egypt to escape Herod (Matthew 2:13-14).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Joseph turned aside into Galilee; the brethren sent Saul to Caesarea, and soldiers took Paul there by night (Matthew 2:22; Acts 9:30; 23:23).

answers.name: Turkey
answers.fact: Saul was sent to Tarsus; scattered disciples reached Antioch; Paul and Barnabas fled to Lystra and Derbe (Acts 9:30; 11:19; 14:6).

answers.name: Cyprus
answers.fact: Disciples scattered by the persecution over Stephen travelled as far as Cyprus (Acts 11:19).

answers.name: Greece
answers.fact: The brethren sent Paul and Silas away by night to Berea, then brought Paul to Athens (Acts 17:10-15).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: After Stephen's death the church was scattered through Judea and Samaria (Acts 8:1).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: The scattered disciples also reached Phenice, the Phoenician coast of today's Lebanon (Acts 11:19).

answers.name: North Macedonia
answers.fact: When the Jews laid wait for Paul, he turned back through Macedonia, the region BD Macedonia places north of Achaia and south of the Balkan Mountains (Acts 20:3).

prompts.display_text: Pin a country or territory whose very first stake of the Church was organized between 1970 and 1973
prompts.text_original: In the early 1970s the Church organized the first stakes in several lands in Asia, Africa, Latin America and the Pacific. A country or territory whose very first stake of the Church was organized between 1970 and 1973.
prompts.citation: Global Histories chronologies and overviews (Peru, Japan, South Africa, French Polynesia, Chile, South Korea, El Salvador, Philippines)
prompts.note: American Samoa (1969), Tonga (1968) and Denmark (1974) fall just outside. The Philippines' first stake came in May 1973.
prompts.summary: In 1970 the Church organized the first stakes in Peru, Japan and South Africa, Tokyo's being the first in Asia. Tahiti and Santiago, Chile followed in 1972, and in 1973 Seoul, San Salvador and Manila gained the first stakes in South Korea, El Salvador and the Philippines.

answers.name: Japan
answers.fact: The Tokyo Stake, the first stake in Asia, was organized March 15, 1970, with Kenji Tanaka as president.

answers.name: Chile
answers.fact: The Santiago Chile Stake, the first in Chile, was organized November 19, 1972.

answers.name: South Korea
answers.fact: The Seoul Korea Stake, the first in mainland Asia, was organized March 8, 1973, with Rhee Ho Nam as president.

answers.name: Peru
answers.fact: The Lima Stake was organized February 22, 1970, with Roberto Vidal as president.

answers.name: Philippines
answers.fact: Elder Ezra Taft Benson organized the Manila Philippines Stake, the first in the country, May 20, 1973, with Augusto A. Lim as president.

answers.name: South Africa
answers.fact: The Transvaal Stake, the first in South Africa, was organized in Johannesburg, March 22, 1970.

answers.name: French Polynesia
answers.fact: The Tahiti Stake, the first in French Polynesia, was organized at Papeete, May 14, 1972.

answers.name: El Salvador
answers.fact: The San Salvador Stake was created June 3, 1973, with Mario Edmundo Scheel as president.
